item.title: New House Democrats Threaten Harvard Boycott Over Union Strike
item.description: More than four dozen incoming House Democrats said they plan to skip a traditional Harvard University orientation for new members of Congress, citing an ongoing strike by the university’s graduate students’ union.
item.dc:creator: Derek Wallbank

item.title: Japan’s Sales Tax Cut Plans Could Stall On No-Confidence Motion
item.description: Japan’s opposition parties plan to submit a motion of no confidence against Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi’s education minister, complicating her efforts to push a sales tax cut bill through parliament in time for it to take effect as planned in April.
item.dc:creator: Sakura Murakami

item.title: What Jensen Huang’s Second Act Means for AI
item.description:
Jensen Huang’s shock return as CEO, courtesy of President Donald Trump and Nvidia’s board, has many wondering what this sudden turn of events means for the chipmaker and the future of AI.
(Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Nvidia’s Huang To Face Scrutiny on Capitol Hill
item.description: "Balance of Power" focuses on the intersection of politics and global business. On today's show, Rep. Greg Stanton, a Democrat from Arizona who serves on the House Foreign Affairs and China Select committees, says Nvidia’s board should testify as Congress investigates Jensen Huang and the company. Former Defense Secretary Mark Esper discusses the national security questions surrounding Nvidia and China, the Trump administration’s options in Iran and the widening war in Ukraine. California Attorney General Rob Bonta says his office will press ahead with its civil investigation of Nvidia, arguing US Attorney General Todd Blanche appeared to have “prejudged” the company’s conduct by calling it a “good corporate citizen.” Dell Chief Financial Officer David Kennedy discusses the company’s record third-quarter results, its $132 billion AI backlog and its outlook for continued growth in AI infrastructure. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Trump Says Huang Pardon ‘Always an Option,’ New York Post Says
item.description: President Donald Trump said a pardon for the reinstated Nvidia Corp. chief Jensen Huang, who testifies before Congress next week, was “always an option,” while adding that he didn’t think such an extraordinary act would be necessary, the New York Post reported Tuesday night.
item.dc:creator: John Harney

item.title: California Nvidia Probe Goes On After CEO Return, Bonta Says
item.description: California Attorney General Rob Bonta blasted the federal government’s handling of the scandal involving Nvidia Corp. and Chief Executive Officer Jensen Huang, saying that he will continue with his own investigation.
item.dc:creator: Anthony Aarons

item.title: Bonta Says Blanche ‘Prejudged’ Nvidia Conduct
item.description: California Attorney General Rob Bonta says his office will press ahead with its civil investigation of Nvidia, arguing US Attorney General Todd Blanche appeared to have “prejudged” the company’s conduct by calling it a “good corporate citizen.” Bonta says California has subpoenaed Nvidia to determine whether China obtained advanced chips or confidential information and whether the company misled investors and the public. He speaks with Kailey Leinz and Joe Mathieu on Bloomberg’s "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Esper on Nvidia, Iran and Ukraine
item.description: Former Defense Secretary Mark Esper discusses the national security questions surrounding Nvidia and China, the Trump administration’s options in Iran and the widening war in Ukraine. Esper, managing partner at Red Cell Partners, says economic pressure on Tehran needs more time to work and calls for a longer-term strategy if the US returns to military action. He speaks with Kailey Leinz and Joe Mathieu on Bloomberg’s "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Rep. Stanton: Nvidia Board, Huang Owe Congress Answers
item.description: Rep. Greg Stanton, a Democrat from Arizona who serves on the House Foreign Affairs and China Select committees, says Nvidia’s board should testify as Congress investigates Jensen Huang and the company. Stanton, who will take part in Huang’s closed-door interview next week, says the House should also get answers from Huang in a public hearing. He speaks with Kailey Leinz and Joe Mathieu on Bloomberg’s "Balance of Power." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: California AG Sees 'Bright Red Flags' Regarding Nvidia
item.description: "When there's flags in the air you have to look," California Attorney General Rob Bonta says about the state's investigation into whether Nvidia illegally sold advanced chips to China and misled investors about the conduct. He speaks on "Balance of Power: Evening Edition." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Younger People Indicating Higher Spending This Holiday Season: The Conference Board’s Dana Peterson
item.description: Dana Peterson says consumers reported stronger views of current conditions and improved expectations for business activity, jobs and income. The survey ran from Nov. 1–17, overlapping with the midterm elections: optimism rose notably among Democrats and independents, while Republicans remained the most optimistic but became somewhat less so. Respondents also saw jobs as more plentiful and easier to find, a view Peterson said fits a labor market marked by limited hiring and firing. She speaks with Romaine Bostick on "The Close." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Bloomberg Businessweek Daily Podcast: Nvidia Euphoria Fades
item.description:
The people, companies and trends shaping the global economy. Watch Carol and Tim LIVE every day on YouTube: http://bit.ly/3vTiACF
On today’s episode: Eric Weiner, Bloomberg News Senior Equities Editor and Michael Ball, Bloomberg News Macro Strategist Dorothy Lund, Columbia Law School Professor Timna Tanners, Managing Director of Equity Research at Wells Fargo Ari Morcos, CEO at Datology (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Milei tendría votos en Senado para aprobar reforma electoral
item.description: Argentina podría suspender las PASO antes de las elecciones de 2027. Bullrich afirma que la reforma cuenta con apoyo suficiente.
item.dc:creator: Manuela Tobias and Patrick Gillespie

item.title: Canada Signs Foreign Investment Deal With Qatar to Lure Capital
item.description: Canada has signed a foreign investment promotion and protection agreement with Qatar, the latest move in Prime Minister Mark Carney’s effort to attract global capital and boost exports to non-US markets.
item.dc:creator: Brian Platt

item.title: Trump’s Higher Education Crackdown Runs Into New Resistance
item.description: The Democrats’ midterm victories give college presidents and higher ed lobbyists a potential lifeline.
item.dc:creator: Liam Knox

item.title: Milei Senate Chief Bullrich Confident Argentina Electoral Reform Will Pass
item.description: A reform in Argentina that would suspend next year’s primary election before the presidential race has the votes it needs to pass this week, Senator Patricia Bullrich said in an interview.
item.dc:creator: Manuela Tobias and Patrick Gillespie

item.title: Huawei Found Guilty of US Criminal Charges in Landmark Case
item.description: Huawei Technologies Co., China’s largest technology company, was found guilty of multiple US criminal charges, including money laundering, a conspiracy to steal trade secrets and defrauding banks about its business in Iran and North Korea.
item.dc:creator: Patricia Hurtado

item.title: Houthi Attack on Riyadh Tower Injures 11 People, Saudis Say
item.description: The Houthis injured 11 people with an attack on a tower in Riyadh’s main business district, Saudi Arabian authorities said, in a further setback to the kingdom’s efforts to establish the capital as a global financial center.
item.dc:creator: Ahmed Elimam, Mirette Magdy and Sherif Tarek

item.title: McCormick Warns of ‘Slippery Slope’ After Trump Pressured Nvidia
item.description: Republican Senator Dave McCormick warned that President Donald Trump’s intervention with the Nvidia Corp. board to reinstate Jensen Huang as chief executive could create a “slippery slope.”
item.dc:creator: Erik Wasson and Annmarie Hordern

item.title: Xi Probes Shanghai Boss, Widening Biggest Shakeup in Decades
item.description: China opened an investigation into Chen Jining, a member of the country’s elite Politburo and the party chief of the financial hub Shanghai — deepening upheaval in the nation’s top leadership as the ruling Communist Party prepares for a reshuffle next year.
item.dc:creator: Bloomberg News
